iteration_summaries.hypothesis: The system has 4 outputs with distinct causal structures. Y3=f(X1,X3) only, with X3 as dominant linear driver and X1 showing saturation. Y4=f(X1,X2,X4,X6) with X2 dominant positive (diminishing returns), X4 moderate positive, X6 negative, X1 negligible. Y2=f(X1,X2,X3,X4,X6) with X2 strong positive, X3 strong negative, X4 moderate positive, X1 weak negative, and a critical X2*X6 sign-flip interaction (X6 increases Y2 at low X2 but decreases Y2 at high X2). X5 negligible for Y2. Y1=f(all 6) is most complex: X2 and X4 are strongest drivers with strong X2*X4 multiplicative interaction (X4 effect 2-5x stronger at high X2); X5 has sigmoid threshold at ~0.4; X5*X6 sign-flip interaction (X6 hurts Y1 when X5<0.35 but helps significantly when X5>0.45); X1 and X3 are weak positive contributors. The main Pareto trade-off is primarily driven by X2 (increases Y1 and Y4 but worsens Y2) and secondarily by X6 at high X2 (increases Y1, decreases Y2, but decreases Y4). Universal optima: X1=1, X3=1, X4=1, X5≈0.55. Y4 max≈0.322 appears to be a ceiling. Y1 max≈1.12 at full settings.
new_findings: Pareto front has 13 non-dominated points with HV=0.263, structured along two main axes: X2 sweep at X6=0.1 and X6 sweep at X2=1.0
Local gradients at [1,1,1,1,0.55,0.1] confirm X6 gradient for Y2 is -0.145 (strongly beneficial) while Y4 is -0.104 (harmful), creating the Y2-vs-Y4 trade-off at high X2
At [1,0.5,1,1,0.55,0.1], X2 gradient for Y4 is 0.332 vs 0.158 at X2=1.0, confirming strong diminishing returns in X2→Y4
Y4 ceiling of ~0.322 is confirmed: all gradients at the best Y4 point are at boundaries or zero for remaining inputs
The X2*X4 interaction strength is confirmed: X4 gradient for Y1 is 0.86 at X2=1.0 but only 0.34 at X2=0.5 (2.5x ratio)
Large gaps exist in the Pareto front between X2=0.4 and X2=0.75, and between X6=0.1 and X6=0.5 at X2=1.0, which could significantly improve HV if filled
surprises: X6 gradient for Y1 at [1,1,1,1,0.55,0.1] is -0.045 (slightly negative), yet global data shows Y1 increases from 0.947 to 1.122 as X6 goes from 0.1 to 1.0. This indicates strong nonlinearity in X6's effect on Y1 — the effect reverses or accelerates at higher X6 values
X6 gradient for Y2 at moderate X2 (0.5) is +0.093 but at high X2 (1.0) is -0.145, confirming the X2*X6 sign-flip interaction for Y2 is quite dramatic
iteration_summaries.next_plan: With 10 remaining evaluations, fill the two largest gaps in the Pareto front: (1) X2 gap between 0.4-0.75 at X6=0.1 using X2=0.5 and 0.6, (2) X2 gap between 0.75-1.0 at X6=0.1 using X2=0.85 and 0.95, (3) X6 gap between 0.1-0.5 at X2=1.0 using X6=0.2 and 0.35, (4) X6 gap between 0.5-1.0 at X2=1.0 using X6=0.75, and (5) diagonal Pareto points at mixed X2/X6 to fill the interior surface of the 3D front.

iteration_summaries.hypothesis: The system has 4 outputs with distinct causal structures. Y3=f(X1,X3) only — X3 is the dominant linear driver (gradient 0.50) with X1 providing moderate positive effect with saturation. Y4=f(X1,X2,X4,X6) — X2 is the dominant positive driver (gradient 0.16-0.26 with diminishing returns), X4 moderate positive (0.11-0.17), X6 moderate negative (-0.06 to -0.11), X1 negligible (0.004). Y2=f(X1,X2,X3,X4,X6) — X2 strong positive (0.16-0.42), X3 strongest negative (-0.06 to -0.10), X4 moderate positive (0.06-0.25), X1 weak negative, X5 negligible; critical X2*X6 sign-flip interaction where X6 increases Y2 at low X2 but decreases Y2 at high X2 (crossover around X2≈0.75). Y1=f(all 6) is the most complex: X2 and X4 are dominant with strong multiplicative X2*X4 interaction (X4 effect 2x stronger at X2=1 vs X2=0.65); X5 has extremely sharp sigmoid threshold at ~0.5 with complete saturation above ~0.55; X5*X6 sign-flip interaction (X6 negative when X5<0.35, strongly positive when X5>0.45); X1 and X3 are weak positive contributors. The Pareto trade-off is primarily driven by X2 (increases Y1,Y4 but worsens Y2) and by X6 at high X2 (increases Y1, decreases both Y2 and Y4). Universal optima: X1=1, X3=1, X4=1, X5≈0.55.
